blocks.text: Designed by two guest curators, the Voices sector, launched in 2024, strengthens a curatorial approach at the heart of the fair. For its third edition, it will address the theme of The Disappearance under the curatorship of Zasha Colah and Francesco Zanot. The Voices sector is presented in a dedicated space in the nave.
The Disappearance

As photography prepares to celebrate its Bicentennial, the medium finds itself in a paradoxical position. Conceived, among other things, as a tool for keeping a record of what would otherwise vanish, photography is celebrated today even as its traditional form seems increasingly unstable, transformed and disrupted by processes that alter its nature and status.

This paradox is the starting point of the curatorial approach for this section. Implicitly referring to the surviving image traditionally associated with the origin of photography— View from the Window at Le Gras —the project rethinks an anniversary that could also be read as a threshold: between commemoration and obsolescence, between mourning and renewal. In this sense, the history of photography becomes inseparable from the cultural, political and material conditions of disappearance.

This section explores disappearance through multiple perspectives and temporalities. It brings together historical works produced to keep a record of subjects, places and phenomena destined to disappear, and contemporary practices that use photography to resist the marginalization of vulnerable communities, endangered landscapes and fragile social realities. Other artists approach disappearance as a material process, creating works designed to alter, fade or self-destruct over time. Others push photography beyond its conventional limits by combining it with painting, sculpture, installation or other languages and disciplines, to the point where the photographic image becomes barely discernible. Particular attention is also paid to practices rooted in algorithmic editing, software manipulation and artificial intelligence, through which images retain a photographic appearance while increasingly disrupting their indexical relationship with reality.

By bringing together historical and contemporary practices, as well as works belonging to classical photography and hybrid visual languages, this selection invites reflection on the notion of disappearance not only as a subject represented by photography, but also as a condition increasingly affecting the medium.
About the Curators
Zasha Colah From India curator and writer.

Since 2023, she has been co-artistic director of Ar/Ge Kunst, the art center in Bolzano. She co-directs Novellas , a series of publications devoted to experimental writing, and contributes to the podcast POST IT (Rai Alto Adige, Rai Radio 1).

She has notably curated the 13th Berlin Biennale (2025), the 2nd Yinchuan Biennale (2018, as part of the curatorial team led by Marco Scotini) and the 3rd Pune Biennale (2017, with Luca Cerizza). She has taught comparative curatorial studies at NABA in Milan since 2018 and sits on the editorial board of Geoarchivi (Meltemi & NABA), a collection devoted to reactivating critical archives at different geopolitical scales. She is currently a visiting fellow at the Städelschule (2025–2026), where she teaches processual and performative sculptural practices and their implications for contemporary forms of exhibition.

Francesco Zanot is an Italian curator, author and photography educator. Former chief curator of Camera in Turin (2015–2017), he has conceived numerous exhibitions and publications devoted to artists such as Boris Mikhailov, Francesco Jodice, Takashi Homma, Erik Kessels, Linda Fregni Nagler and Luigi Ghirri. His texts have been published in several monographs, and with Alec Soth he is the author of Ping Pong Conversations . He directs the Master’s in Photography at NABA in Milan and regularly lectures at international institutions, including Columbia University (New York), ECAL (Lausanne), IUAV (Venice) and the Universidad Politécnica de Valencia. A member of the curatorial platform Fantom since its founding, he notably curated the inaugural exhibitions Give Me Yesterday and Stefano Graziani: Questioning Pictures at the Fondazione Prada Osservatorio in Milan. Since 2019, he has been artistic director of the Foto/Industria Biennale, organized by the MAST Foundation in Bologna. His latest book, Irrational , co-written with Francesco Jodice, was published in the summer 2025.
